facts.fact_text: All the applicants accepted that they had participated in legally organised demonstrations.
The applicants denied having chanted illegal slogans or slogans in favour of an illegal organisation during the demonstrations.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted that the applicants had participated in a demonstration organised by trade unions and non-governmental organisations held on 17 December 2005 with the authorisation of the governor's office.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted that the applicants had participated in a demonstration organised by trade unions and non-governmental organisations held on 19 February 2006 with the authorisation of the governor's office.
On 6 March 2006 the applicants were taken into police custody.
The applicants were taken into police custody on suspicion of aiding and abetting the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).
The applicants were questioned about various CDs, documents, books and periodicals that had allegedly been found by the police in their homes.
The applicants were charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 220 § 7 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).
The applicants were charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Deniz Bakır of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Metin Kürekçi of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Necla Çomak of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Alihan Alhan of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

The remaining applicants (other than Deniz Bakır, Metin Kürekçi, Necla Çomak and Alihan Alhan) were convicted on 17 January 2007 of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

The remaining applicants convicted of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation were each sentenced to one year and eight months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

At the material time, Article 220 § 7 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who aids an illegal organisation knowingly and willingly, even if he does not belong to the hierarchical structure of the organisation, shall be punished as a member of the organisation.

At the material time, Article 220 § 8 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who spreads propaganda for the organisation or its objectives shall be punished by a term of imprisonment of between one and three years, and if the crime is committed through the press or other media, the sentence shall be increased by one half.

The Human Rights Watch report of 1 November 2010 stated that Turkish Penal Code Articles 220/6 and 220/7 are so vaguely worded and lacking in clarity about what is prohibited as to offer an individual no indication of how to regulate or limit conduct.
The MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) was classified as an illegal armed organisation.
According to information on the Internet, the ESP (the Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and the SGD (Socialist Youth Association) were connected to the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).
